name: opponent_forcing_moves
idea: The opponent has many forcing moves available next turn, especially checks and profitable captures, so the side to move is under pressure to react and may lose material or the initiative even when a calm static eval looks acceptable.

name: king_escape_squares
idea: A king with few safe adjacent flight squares is vulnerable to checks, back-rank mates, and mating nets; the network penalizes low king mobility even when no immediate mate is in the classical features.

name: attacked_knight_tempo
idea: A knight under attack, especially by a pawn or king, often has to retreat and cedes the initiative; the network values how many safe retreat squares the knight has and penalizes a kicked knight with few good squares.

name: enemy_king_stuck_in_center
idea: With queens on the board, a king stuck on the central e/d-file and still holding castling rights is a lasting tactical liability; the side to move is more optimistic when its own king is safer and the enemy king has not escaped.

name: pawn_tempo_on_high_piece
idea: A pawn break that attacks a queen, rook, or minor piece gains time and can be stronger than static evaluation suggests, especially in open early-middlegame positions.

name: forcing_initiative
idea: The side to move has a forcing resource: a capture, check, or one-move attack on a loose high-value piece. This initiative is worth more than the static classical estimate, because it forces the opponent to react.

name: opponent_pawn_on_seventh
idea: An enemy pawn one square from promotion is a decisive threat that raw material counts miss. Even if the side to move has checking resources, the opponent's queening pawn means the position is much worse than classical evaluation suggests.

name: opponent_checks_available
idea: The number of legal checking moves the opponent has. A high count means our king is dangerously exposed and the opponent can force the play, which explains why the network is more pessimistic than a static evaluation that only counts attacks on the king zone.

name: opponent_pieces_in_our_half
idea: The number of non-pawn, non-king opponent pieces that have penetrated into our half of the board. Enemy rooks, bishops, knights, and queens deep in our territory create threats and restrictions that a pure material or space count underestimates.

name: king_trap_check_pressure
idea: A cramped enemy king turns ordinary checks into mating threats. The network rewards checks that hit a king with few safe flight squares, an interaction that raw check counts and king-zone attack counts miss.

name: forcing_double_threat
idea: One forcing move can create two problems: check or capture plus an attack on another valuable piece. The network values this tactical overlap more than static material and separate check/capture counts.

name: back_rank_heavy_pressure
idea: Rooks and queens penetrating to the opponent's first two ranks, especially against a king with blocked or covered flight squares, create back-rank mating-net pressure that ordinary material and open-file scores underrate.

name: protected_checking_sacrifice
idea: A check is much more dangerous when the checking piece is protected, because the king cannot simply capture it; queen and knight checks landing on defended squares often force a mating net or win material.

name: pin_to_king_capturable_by_low_value
idea: An enemy piece pinned to its king is a real tactical target when it is also attacked by our king or a pawn, because it cannot move and can be taken by a low-value piece.

name: knight_king_zone_pressure
idea: Knights aimed at the enemy king zone are a concrete attacking asset; a knight attacking squares next to the king or key weak squares often creates mating threats that static evaluation misses.

name: development_deficit
idea: The side to move has more pieces still on their starting squares than the opponent. In open positions with many pieces, this undeveloped state lets the opponent seize the initiative, so the network is more pessimistic than a classical count of material and mobility suggests.

name: early_queen_sortie_penalty
idea: Moving the queen out early while minor pieces remain undeveloped is a classic opening mistake. The opponent can gain tempos by attacking the queen, leaving the side to move behind in development. The network penalizes this lost time more heavily than classical concepts.

name: tactical_pressure_against_us
idea: The opponent's pieces are actively attacking your pieces, forcing you to react and make defensive or retreating moves. This constant tactical pressure is a form of initiative that the network values more negatively than a classical evaluation, even when no piece is immediately hanging.

name: multi_target_forcing_pressure
idea: The network rewards a position when the side to move has a legal move that creates several immediate targets at once: checking, capturing, or attacking multiple enemy pieces with the moving piece. A quiet-looking move that points at two or more enemy units is treated as real pressure, not just mobility.

name: capture_fork_material
idea: The network values a capture that does more than win the captured piece: the capturing piece stays on a square where it forks or attacks several other valuable enemy units. This is the extra material the opponent cannot save after the capture, which static material and ordinary mobility miss.

name: latent_castling_resource
idea: The network treats an unused, legal castling option as a latent king-safety and rook-activation asset, especially when the king is still in the centre and the opponent no longer has the same resource. The side that can still castle later has a free tempo in reserve, even if the best move right now is not castling.

name: connected_advanced_pawn_mass
idea: In endgames, two adjacent advanced pawns create breakthrough and queening chances that are greater than the sum of two loose pawns; the network values the pawn phalanx itself, not just formally passed pawns.

name: king_escort_of_passed_pawn
idea: A passed pawn is much more dangerous when its own king is close enough to protect it and shepherd it toward promotion, especially if the enemy king is far from the pawn's path.

name: rook_cutoff_of_advanced_passer
idea: An active rook can be worth much more than its material when it cuts the enemy king off from an advanced passed pawn, either by controlling an intervening file or by controlling the queening rank.
